subject: Post-call: Latency & throughput benchmarks / next A-B tests vs hyperscaler
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@globex.com>, Samantha Lee <sam.lee@globex.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: latency & throughput scoping / next steps

Thanks for a great call today — quick recap and proposed next steps.

Summary from our discovery:
- Goal: validate sustained p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec for your inference-heavy recommendation pipeline (sequence lengths ~512 typical, some up to 2k).
- Current constraint: must hit p95 < 220ms for 512-token calls, and sustain >= 2500 tokens/sec aggregate for burst windows.
- Priority models: open-gpt-2-large (internal name: gpt-2l), and one fine-tuned recommendation model.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a representative set of requests (anonymized) — we can use these in an A/B harness.
2) Redwood will run an A/B test vs the hyperscaler endpoint you're evaluating (we'll match model variant, sequence lengths, and batching).
3) We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens for each configuration.
4) Schedule: aim to run the first A/B overnight on Wed (UTC) so you have results Thu morning.

Attachments: sample payload format and an ops checklist (attached).

Open questions from our side:
- Do you have a preferred traffic shape (steady vs bursts) and any SLO windows we should target for the canary?
- Any IP/egress constraints for test harness hitting your hyperscaler endpoints?

If that plan looks good I'll loop in Rishi (SRE/bench lead) and Neha (solutions) to align the test harness.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency & throughput scoping / next steps

Marissa — thanks for the recap, that matches our internal notes. Quick answers and a few early results we ran this morning:

Traffic shape: primary is bursty (30s-2min bursts when recommendations are generated), with sustained low baseline. Please include both steady-state and burst profiles.
SLO windows: p95 < 220ms for 512 tokens, p99 < 450ms is our target.

Preliminary numbers (our internal quick test vs HyperscalerA endpoint):
- HyperscalerA (region us-west-2, single-shard): 512 tokens, batch=1 -> p95=340ms, p99=820ms, tokens/sec ~ 1,800
- HyperscalerA with batching (batch=4): p95=280ms, p99=710ms, tokens/sec ~ 3,600 (but tail still high)

We can share anonymized payloads — attaching two sample sets. Also FYI, procurement needs a short performance note for our infra team before we let external test harnesses call our endpoints; happy to provide limited credentials or a temporary NATed IP range.

Attaching: globex-test-payloads.jsonl (anonymized)

Daniel
Daniel Park
Principal ML Engineer, Globex Corp

Thanks Marissa / Daniel — I'm good to run the harness. Technical notes / plan: 

1) Harness: we'll use the Redwood bench-runner (link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/globex-bench-harness) to replay globex-test-payloads.jsonl with configurable concurrency and traffic shape.
2) Configs: default to continuous batching with a 20ms batching window to preserve latency SLOs; we'll also run fixed micro-batching (batch sizes 1/2/4) to compare.
3) Model parity: we'll use the same model weights you specified. For HyperscalerA we'll hit the endpoint you provided and match request params.
4) Metrics: p50/p95/p99, 95/99%-ile CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and per-token infra cost. We'll include histograms and tail traces for requests > p99.
5) Long-seq tests: for 2048 tokens we'll run 30-minute steady runs and 5x burst spikes to capture memory pressure effects.

Operational asks for Globex: please provide the allowlisted IPs or temporary credentials for HyperscalerA endpoint by EOD Tue so we can start Wed 00:00 UTC. Also confirm any egress limits.

I'll push raw logs + processed charts to the shared Drive folder and a short .ppt with highlights.

Rishi
